chunk_findings.detail: The new check tests for the substring `'id="D1"'` anywhere in the brief, not for a record whose actual `id` attribute is `D1`. Given a task whose files include `ledger/core/money.py` (`governs_d1` is true) but whose brief omits the D1 record and instead contains another record or text that merely mentions `related_id="D1"` (for example `<ddflow-record kind="decision" id="D2" related_id="D1">...`), the substring is present, so `('id="D1"' in brief) == governs_d1` is true and the check passes even though the governing D1 decision was not surfaced. This is the same class of false pass the fix was supposed to remove.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_support.py:32

chunk_findings.detail: The predicate still does a raw substring search, not token matching. For a D1-governed file, `work(sc, client, tmp_path, wt_root, "P1.T1", {"ledger/core/money.py": "x=1"})` with a brief such as `<ddflow-record kind="decision" data-id="D1">` gives `('id="D1"' in brief)` as `True` because the substring appears inside `data-id="D1"`; `governs_d1` is also `True`, so the check passes even though no `id` attribute contains `D1`. That contradicts the comment's "match that token, not the bare substring" and leaves a false-positive bypass of the brief check for this input.
chunk_findings.title: demos/lifecycle_support.py:32

chunk_findings.detail: The `work` function in `demos/lifecycle_support.py` uses the local variable `files` inside the `governs_d1` check before `files` is defined in the execution flow. Looking at `demos/lifecycle_support.py`, `brief = client.tool("ddflow_brief", item=item)[0]` occurs at line 21, and the `files` parameter is only unpacked or iterated over later in the function (at `for rel, body in files.items():` on line 38), leading to an immediate `NameError: name 'files' is not defined` when `work()` is invoked with a `files` argument.

chunk_findings.detail: The new table assertion can pass vacuously. It slices `inspect.getsource(MC)` from the first occurrence of `RESOURCES: tuple` to the first occurrence of `RESOURCE_BY_URI`, but it never checks that the end marker is after the start marker or that the resulting slice is non-empty. For example, if `_core.py` contains `RESOURCE_BY_URI` in a module docstring, comment, or forward annotation before the actual `RESOURCES` tuple, then `start > end`, `table` becomes `""`, and `assert "fold(" not in table and "EventLog" not in table` passes even if the real resource table contains `fold(` or `EventLog`. It also no longer checks the `RESOURCE_BY_URI` mapping line itself or any code between that line and `class Server`, so a violation such as `RESOURCE_BY_URI = {r.uri: r for r in RESOURCES if not fold(r)}` would be missed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_roborev_findings.py::test_every_mcp_resource_is_served_through_the_cli

chunk_findings.detail: The added comment asserts that monkeypatching `ddflow.infra.log.install_kind` now reaches the same name that both `upgrade_remedy` and `skew_message` call, but the diff only inserts the call-time `from . import install_kind` inside `upgrade_remedy`. `skew_message` in the same module is not changed, so it still calls the `install_kind` object bound at import time. A caller or regression test that monkeypatches `ddflow.infra.log.install_kind` and then invokes `ddflow.infra.log.skew_message(...)` will still observe the pre-patch install kind, so the pre-split behavior remains broken for one of the two promised functions.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/log/_skew.py:41

chunk_findings.detail: The added `assert start < end` only rejects the case where the first `RESOURCE_BY_URI` occurs before the first `RESOURCES: tuple`; it still slices to the first occurrence of the marker. If `_core.py` has a docstring or comment before the real definitions that mentions both markers in order, e.g. `"""RESOURCES: tuple ... RESOURCE_BY_URI ..."""`, then both `start` and `end` are inside that docstring, `start < end` passes, and `table` is just the docstring fragment. The real `RESOURCES` tuple after the docstring can contain `fold(` or `EventLog`, but those characters are outside the slice, so the assertion passes and the test falsely proves the table is clean.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_roborev_findings.py::test_every_mcp_resource_is_served_through_the_cli

chunk_findings.detail: Replacing `index` with `rindex` still does not anchor the slice to the real module-level definitions; it only selects the last textual occurrence of each marker. If `_core.py` contains a trailing comment, docstring, or later function that mentions both marker strings in order, e.g. `# RESOURCES: tuple is indexed by RESOURCE_BY_URI`, then `start` and `end` land in that trailing text, `table` becomes only that fragment, and the `fold(` / `EventLog` assertion can pass even when the actual `RESOURCES` table contains `fold(` or `EventLog`. Conversely, if a later helper mentions `RESOURCE_BY_URI` and legitimately contains `fold(` or `EventLog`, `end` extends into that helper and the test fails even though the resource table is clean. The earlier vacuous-slice concern is therefore not fully answered by using `rindex`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_roborev_findings.py:317-318

chunk_findings.detail: The `rindex` change still does not ensure the slice is the real `RESOURCES` table. `rindex` finds the last textual occurrence anywhere in `inspect.getsource(MC)`, including post-definition comments or string literals. For example, if `_core.py` ends with a comment like `# Keep RESOURCES: tuple above in sync with RESOURCE_BY_URI.` after the real table, then `start` and `end` both point inside that comment, `start < end` passes, and `table` is `" above in sync with "`. The real table earlier could contain `fold(` and `EventLog` and the test would still pass, so the regression test can still be defeated by a trailing marker mention.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_roborev_findings.py:316-317

chunk_findings.detail: The new test invokes `ddflow_cli(repo, "pins", "regenerate", "--approval", "request")` without `--agent` (or any agent marker), so it does not exercise the intended agent approval path. In `_regenerate_approval`, a non-agent `agent` causes the fixed code to return `O.refused("pins", "--approval is an agent's route; a person re-records directly")`, which contains neither `"pins.regenerate"` nor `"requested"`; the test’s `assert "requested"` therefore fails before proving the reported bug is fixed. chunk_findings.detail: The new `EC.commit_at` can advance `wt.base` after `landed_before` has already been captured on the preceding line. When the primary has an uncommitted shard, `EC.commit_at` creates a new commit on the base branch before `W.merge` runs. If the merge then fails (for example, the existing conflict path where `c.txt` conflicts), `_landed_anyway` is called with the stale pre-event SHA while the base has already moved to the event commit. The branch has not landed—the modified test still asserts `main:c.txt` is unchanged—but the landing-check helper receives a baseline that no longer represents the state before the merge attempt, so it can misclassify the failure or report a false “landed anyway” note. The event commit should happen before `landed_before` is read, or `landed_before` should be refreshed after `EC.commit_at`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:188

chunk_findings.detail: `EC.commit_at` runs before `W.merge` and does not know whether the merge will succeed. In the refusal case with a primary event shard plus a `c.txt` conflict, `main` gets a new shard commit and only then `W.merge` returns `REFUSED`; the CLI reports failure but the primary branch has moved. The change acknowledges this by deleting the old `rev-parse HEAD` equality assertion in `tests/test_merge_primary_clean.py` and replacing it with a weaker `main:c.txt` content check, so a failed merge no longer guarantees the primary was left where it was.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:188

chunk_findings.detail: `EC.commit_at(log, cfg, "merge", f"merge {item}")` is called unconditionally during `merge` even when the merge will ultimately fail due to file conflicts (such as in `test_merge_primary_clean` where `c.txt` conflicts). This causes the primary's uncommitted event shards to be committed to `main` as part of a failed merge operation, altering the repository state and committing uncommitted work even though the merge itself was refused and rolled back.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/merge.py:186
